item.title: US 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rate hits 7.40%, likely to further erode housing demand
item.description: In the U.S., the 30-year fixed-rate mortgage has surged to 7.40%, fueled by rising inflation that has also driven up energy costs and Treasury yields. With midterm elections looming, the housing market is grappling with affordability challenges. Homeowners are reluctant to sell due to these higher mortgage rates. While home prices remain high, experts forewarn of a potential market stall rather than a significant downturn.

item.title: US President Donald Trump buys $1 million-plus stakes in Meta, Microsoft, McDonald’s; adds SpaceX debt
item.description: Donald Trump invested over $1 million in stocks of several major companies during August. Notable purchases included Meta Platforms, McDonald's, Microsoft, and space-related debt from SpaceX. His investment activities encompass trading in shares of Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices, key players in the AI sector. Trump's financial dealings during his presidency have raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest.

item.title: Infosys, Wipro ADRs fall nearly 3% after TCS earnings, US crackdown on H-1B-linked green card programme
item.description: Infosys and Wipro ADRs fell nearly 3% in US trading as investors assessed TCS’s quarterly results and fresh US immigration restrictions. Concerns over technology spending, AI disruption and tighter employment-based immigration added pressure to Indian IT stocks.

item.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Friday
item.description: Indian markets plunged on Thursday as RBI policy tightening, persistent FII selling, rising bond yields and rupee weakness battered sentiment. The Nifty hit a 52-week low of 22,179, while the Sensex fell 1,045 points, wiping out over Rs 10 lakh crore.

item.title: Market Trading Guide: Deepa Jewellers among 2 stock recommendations for Friday
item.description: Indian markets remained under pressure as hawkish RBI policy, persistent FII outflows, rising bond yields and rupee weakness weighed on sentiment. Amid the sell-off, analysts identified Brooks Laboratories and Deepa Jewellers as medium-term opportunities based on bullish technical breakouts.

item.title: Rs 9,395 crore block deal! GQG exits ITC shares after a sharp 30% crash this year
item.description: ITC witnessed a nearly Rs 9,437 crore block deal as a GQG-linked fund sold 36.51 crore shares, while Fidelity and major Indian mutual funds bought stakes. The transaction comes as ITC shares remain under pressure from taxation concerns and weak volume recovery.

item.title: US stocks: US markets fall as higher yields and oil prices flag inflation risk
item.description: US stocks fell as crude oil prices surged and Treasury yields remained high, raising inflation concerns. Major companies like Amazon, Tesla, and Nvidia experienced losses, contributing to a broader decline in the technology sector. Investors are now focused on upcoming third-quarter earnings reports, particularly from financial institutions. The Federal Reserve is expected to keep interest rates unchanged in October, while considering future hikes.

item.title: US jobless claims hover near 57-year low for fourth consecutive week
item.description: In a recent report, weekly unemployment claims saw a slight drop of 2,000, totaling 197,000, which suggests some stability within the job market. Nonetheless, nonfarm payroll growth remained disappointing, with just 29,000 jobs created in September. Additionally, there was an increase of 17,000 in ongoing unemployment benefits, highlighting challenges faced by new job seekers amid geopolitical uncertainties and a tightening labor pool.

item.title: Absence of AI in equities will become India's strength in a year, mkts to start attracting flows: CEA
item.description: Chief Economic Advisor V Anantha Nageswaran indicated that India's absence of AI focus might become an advantage. He believes that if the AI boom falters, foreign investors will seek alternative growth opportunities in India. Despite currency depreciation and external challenges, India maintains strong economic fundamentals and growth. Nageswaran highlighted the manageable current account deficit and well-capitalized banking system as positive factors.

item.title: PepsiCo to cut costs as weak North America business hurts annual core profit forecast
item.description: PepsiCo is gearing up to implement further cost-cutting measures in response to rising input costs and a slowdown in consumer demand. CEO Ramon Laguarta indicated that actionable strategies would be rolled out shortly to bolster investments. The company has revised its fiscal 2026 core earnings per share growth estimate to a modest 1% to 2%, down from previous figures, while annual organic revenue growth is now anticipated at approximately 3%.

item.title: China has no need or intention to weaken yuan for trade edge, central bank says
item.description: China's central bank stated it does not intend to depreciate the yuan for competitive trade advantages. It emphasized that the market plays a decisive role in determining exchange rates. The central bank will not set exchange rate targets nor intervene in long-term trends. Starting in 2027, additional foreign exchange data will be reported to the International Monetary Fund.

item.title: Bank of England's Bailey says government debt commitments needed more than ever
item.description: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey highlighted the importance of credible fiscal policies for stabilizing public finances. Rising inflation and high levels of government borrowing put pressure on global bond markets. He emphasized that realistic debt commitments could mitigate demands for higher returns from bond investors. Bailey also noted the need for central banks to focus on reducing inflation.

item.title: RBI's 29-day VRRR auction receives tepid response despite high surplus liquidity
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India on Thursday executed a noteworthy 29-day variable rate reverse repo auction, attracting Rs 79,655 crore in bids, fully accepted at a 5.49 percent rate. This event contrasted sharply with the one-day VRRR auction, which invited bids totaling Rs 1,60,664 crore. Currently, the banking sector enjoys a liquidity surplus of around Rs 4.

item.title: Dow Jones| Nasdaq | US Stock Market Today | Live: Nasdaq plunges over 400 pts as tech stocks slide; high yields fuel inflation fears
M&M, Maruti Suzuki among 6 Sensex stocks that hit 52-week lows and slipped up to 12% in a month
item.description: Seven Sensex stocks touched fresh 52-week lows as Indian equities suffered a sharp sell-off on Thursday. Mahindra & Mahindra and Maruti Suzuki fell around 12% each over the past month, while Bharat Electronics, Power Grid, NTPC and ITC also hit yearly lows.

item.title: India's 10-year yield hits Dec 2023 peak as US debt rout, oil spike hurt
item.description: The Indian government bond market is feeling the heat from escalating US Treasury yields and climbing oil prices. Crude oil has surged, fueled by ongoing fears regarding supply disruptions in the Middle East. In light of this, the Reserve Bank of India has raised its policy rate, signaling a potential tightening of fiscal measures. As a result, forecasts suggest the benchmark 10-year bond yield could hit 7.40%.

item.title: Housing sales may take a hit on higher mortgage rates: CREDAI, NAREDCO
item.description: Realtors' industry bodies CREDAI and NAREDCO have expressed concerns about rising home loan costs. The Reserve Bank of India raised the repo rate by 25 basis points, signaling potential further hikes. This increase could dampen housing sales during the upcoming festive season despite strong underlying demand. Experts believe that long-term buyer sentiment will support the market resilience. Overall, housing demand in major cities showed a slight annual increase recently.

item.title: Market wrap: Infosys, Tech Mahindra, Adani Ent, ITC top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
item.description: Indian markets extended their sell-off as the RBI’s hawkish policy stance pressured rate-sensitive sectors and reset near-term valuations. The Nifty fell 1.64% to 22,231.80, while the Sensex dropped 1.46% to 71,593.24, with metals and realty leading losses.

item.title: Rates, inflation and AI emerge as key risks for global growth: Deutsche Bank Survey
item.description: Rising interest rates and bond yields are the biggest growth risks for wealthy investors, while Asia is seen as the most stable geopolitical region and the US remains the preferred destination for capital allocation.

item.title: India at an inflection point in private credit space: What is creating the opportunity?
TCS dividend! IT giant declares second interim dividend of Rs 12 per share for FY27
item.description: TCS announced a second interim dividend of Rs 12 per share for FY27 after reporting a 15% rise in Q2 net profit to Rs 13,884 crore. Revenue grew 11% to Rs 73,188 crore, while operating margin stood at 24%.

item.title: RBI intervention halts rupee's slide to record low, risks linger
item.description: The Indian rupee struggles amid climbing oil prices and a weakening of Asian currencies. Despite the Reserve Bank of India's intervention, traders remain wary regarding the future of the currency. Many market players doubt that a central bank interest rate hike will stem capital flight, while escalating Brent crude prices raise alarms over possible Middle Eastern supply issues.

item.title: No SIP returns in 2 years? Prashant Jain explains why that's good news for your wealth
TCS Q2 results: Profit rises 15% YoY to Rs 13,884 crore; co declares dividend at Rs 12 per share
item.description: TCS Q2 Results 2026: IT services major Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported 15% year-on-year (YoY) growth in its consolidated net profit at Rs 13,884 crore for the second quarter. Also the company has declared a second interim dividend of Rs 12 per share for the financial year 2026-27.

item.title: Citi’s India IB revenue nearly doubles as bank raises $16 billion for clients, shows data
item.description: Citi’s India investment banking revenue nearly doubled to $52 million, making it the country’s top-ranked investment bank. The lender helped Indian companies raise nearly $16 billion and advised on $36 billion of M&A, driven by overseas expansion and technology-sector activity.

item.title: Global Market: ECB may need further rate hikes as inflation risks remain elevated, Dolenc says
item.description: The ECB may raise interest rates further as inflation risks remain tilted upward, with rates already at 2.5% and inflation at 3.8%. Policymaker Primoz Dolenc cited energy, food and geopolitical risks, while noting stable core inflation. Strong economic growth could add pressure, but rising bond yields pose risks to euro zone activity.

item.title: Global Market: European stocks slide as oil surge revives inflation concerns
item.description: European shares fell as banks hit over three-month lows amid rising bond yields and oil prices. Investors worried persistent inflation could constrain central bank rate cuts and hurt growth, while markets awaited ECB, Federal Reserve and Bank of England signals.

item.title: How to Invest in Gold, copper & other commodities? Praveena Rai of MCX Answers
Adani Group stocks tumble as market rout deepens; Adani Green, Adani Ent, others tank up to 10%
item.description: On October 8, shares of Adani Group experienced sharp declines amid a wider market downturn, with Adani Green Energy plunging by 10% and Adani Enterprises by 7%. Despite receiving a long-term rating upgrade from CARE Ratings, investor confidence remained shaky. Other subsidiaries, including Adani Power and Adani Ports, also witnessed losses, underscoring the market's inherent volatility and investor unease regarding the current economic climate.

item.title: Global Market: Eurozone bond yields surge as energy prices fuel rate hike bets
item.description: Eurozone bond yields rise sharply as higher oil prices fuel inflation concerns and expectations of tighter monetary policy, while widening France-Germany spreads highlight growing fiscal and rate risks.

item.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: Equities aren’t enough? Praveena Rai makes a case for commodities
item.description: In India, commodities are steadily gaining traction as a crucial component of investment strategies. As investors diversify beyond conventional assets, they are discovering opportunities in gold, copper, and energy markets. Innovative financial products make it easy to engage in these commodities without the need for physical possession. Success demands a strong grasp of specific commodities and diligence in choosing regulated trading platforms.

item.title: Inside 11-quarter high earnings pomp, 46 companies may wipe out up to 84% of their Q2 profits
item.description: At least 46 companies are expected to report double-digit profit declines in Q2, despite Motilal Oswal projecting 22% earnings growth for its coverage universe. Autos, cement, healthcare, consumer and cap goods are among sectors facing pressure, highlighting the uneven nature of the September-quarter earnings recovery.

item.title: Vedanta dividend alert! Anil Agarwal-led firm announces Rs 5/share interim dividend for FY27. Check record date
item.description: Vedanta dividend 2026: Vedanta has announced its first interim dividend of Rs 5 per share for FY27, with a total payout of Rs 1,955 crore. The dividend comes after the company’s mega demerger earlier this year. Investors will need to hold Vedanta shares by October 14 to qualify, with October 13 being the last buying day.

item.title: 8 smallcap stocks turned multibaggers in 2026 after crashing over 40% in 2025
item.description: Nine smallcap stocks that fell over 40% in 2025 have more than doubled in 2026, highlighting sharp turnarounds in investor sentiment and emerging as some of the year’s biggest multibagger stories.

item.title: Nifty 50 hits fresh 52-week low! What technical charts indicate as selloff intensifies
item.description: Nifty 50 plunged below 22,200 to a fresh 52-week low as soaring oil prices, persistent FII selling and the RBI’s rate hike weighed on sentiment. Analysts expect near-term pressure to persist, with market direction likely hinging on Q2 earnings, corporate cash flows and key technical levels in the coming sessions.

item.title: Jefferies sees 76% upside in Kalyan Jewellers in bull case; here is why
item.description: Jefferies has reiterated a Buy rating on Kalyan Jewellers, setting a base target of Rs 830 and a bull-case target of Rs 1,000, implying a 76% upside. The brokerage highlighted market-share gains, store additions, and structural shifts to organised retail as primary long-term growth triggers for the stock.

item.title: Germany regains safe haven status as European bond risks mount
item.description: European government bond markets face renewed volatility as investors pull funds from fiscally vulnerable nations like France and Italy. Germany has re-emerged as a primary safe haven, benefiting from capital inflows alongside Dutch, Swiss, and Swedish debt amid rising fiscal and political concerns across the euro zone.

item.title: Mastek shares defy weak markets, gain 3% after Staffordshire County council picks company for Oracle Cloud transformation
item.description: Mastek shares witnessed an uptick on Thursday despite weak market sentiment after its UK subsidiary was selected by Staffordshire County Council for an AI-enabled Oracle Cloud transformation programme. The engagement will cover finance, procurement, human resources and payroll, with Mastek deploying its ADOPT AI platform as the council’s integrated cloud platform.

item.title: Global Market: TSMC third-quarter revenue jumps 50% as AI chip demand surges
item.description: TSMC reports record third-quarter revenue, beating estimates as surging AI demand drives strong growth in advanced chips, while the chipmaker prepares to provide a detailed outlook on earnings, capital spending and AI demand.

item.title: Nilesh Shah on What India Needs to Do to Bring FPIs Back
Multibagger stock! Cupid shares jump 4%, soar 238% in 2026. What's driving the rally?
item.description: Cupid shares rose 3.76% to hit a high of Rs 356.90 on Thursday, extending their rally since the September 30 business update to around 16%. The stock has gained 238.78% in 2026 so far, sharply outperforming the Nifty 50, which is down 14% over the same period.

item.title: Paytm shares crash 10%, wipe off Rs 10,970 crore from m-cap. More pain ahead?
item.description: Paytm shares crashed on Wednesday after reports suggested a possible delay in the rollout of UPI MDR. Analysts said the stock faces immediate support at Rs 1,560-1,550, while a decisive break below could trigger further selling.

item.title: Indian firms seen posting faster profit growth despite global headwinds
item.description: Indian companies are projected to achieve profit growth during the September quarter despite various challenges affecting different sectors. Foreign investors are retreating from Indian stocks, impacting the benchmark Nifty 50 index's performance this year. Strong domestic demand and favorable conditions in certain sectors are expected to sustain earnings growth for many firms. Analysts believe that financials will be a significant driver of earnings, supported by healthy loan growth.

item.title: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: Bear markets can breed best investment ideas, says Nilesh Shah
item.description: Nilesh Shah from Kotak Mutual Fund highlights the advantage of bear markets in uncovering robust investment opportunities. He points out that India's growth potential surpasses that of South Korea due to its remarkable talent pool and infrastructure. Shah advises diversifying portfolios with alternative investments like SIFs, credit AIFs, and global funds, suggesting that 15% to 20% be dedicated to international assets.

item.title: India bonds hemmed in as market digests higher rates
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India has increased its key policy rate by 25 basis points, raising it to 5.50%. This adjustment signifies a strategic step towards cautious monetary tightening shaped by global economic developments. Traders are exercising caution due to heightened global yields and soaring crude oil prices impacting the bond market.

item.title: Global Market: China stocks slide as tech valuations face earnings test
item.description: Chinese stocks fell after the holiday break amid renewed US-China tensions, higher US Treasury yields and concerns over elevated technology valuations. The CSI300 and Shanghai Composite declined, while the STAR 50 suffered sharper losses. Investors are reassessing high-valued chip and technology stocks, with trade tensions, earnings expectations and global yields weighing on sentiment.

item.title: Japanese investors sell foreign bonds for third straight week as Treasury yields jump
item.description: In a significant market shift, Japanese investors have divested from foreign debt for three consecutive weeks amidst climbing domestic yields. As US Treasury yields hit record highs, local bonds present a more appealing alternative. This trend not only sees a resurgence in Japanese stock acquisitions but also marks a recovery in foreign investments into Japanese long-term bonds, reversing earlier outflows.

item.title: TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech, other IT stocks jump up to 3% despite weak market sentiment. What to expect as Q2 earnings season begins?
item.description: IT stocks rose on Thursday as investors turned their attention to TCS, which is set to kick off the Q2 earnings season. Analysts expect modest sequential revenue growth, while a favourable base and margin support could aid year-on-year growth. Currency tailwinds may also support margins across Indian IT services companies.

item.title: Can Applied Digital's AI data-centre growth drive further gains?
item.description: Applied Digital posts a sharp revenue surge in fiscal Q1 2027 as AI data-centre demand drives growth, while expanding US capacity, long-term contracts and a planned Finland campus strengthen its growth pipeline.

item.title: Jefferies cuts target prices for BSE, Turtlemint & other stocks ahead of Q2 results. Check list
item.description: Jefferies has cut target prices for BSE, Turtlemint and several other non-lending financial stocks ahead of Q2 earnings, while retaining Buy ratings on most stocks in its coverage.
